claims.statement: Directory role synchronization completed successfully at 02:10 on 2026-09-29, updating 214 role assignments with no logged errors, but authorization failures on the customer-records app began 6+ hours later at 08:30.
claims.corroboration: Verified tier-1 sources: change record confirms directory job success; helpdesk alert confirms failure timeline divergence from directory change.
claims.limitation: Establishes temporal sequence but not causal link; observability gap (m7_e10) prevents visibility into app's entitlement state.

claims.statement: All 214 affected users reporting 403 access denials are among those whose roles were modified in the overnight directory sync; no 403s reported from users outside this cohort.
claims.corroboration: Support report (tier 2, reviewed) directly correlates failure cohort to directory change cohort.
claims.limitation: Non-authoritative sources; support tickets are proxy impact only (m7_e01 and m7_e11 are tier 2). Requires count_affected_users diagnostic to establish actual scope.

claims.statement: The customer-records app's authorization check is reading stale entitlements (not the 214 updated roles from the directory sync) or has a version mismatch between stored and requested entitlements.
claims.corroboration: Timing gap and observability gap create conditions where a version mismatch could exist undetected. Release r7 (m7_e04) noted no functional changes, reducing likelihood of intentional auth logic change.
claims.limitation: Highly speculative without entitlement introspection. Observability gap (m7_e10) prevents direct confirmation. Alternative causes (IDP claim error, stale cache at different layer) remain open.

capability_gaps.reason: Determine if directory's IDP claims are correctly formatted and reaching the app, vs. app's stored/cached representation
Verify app's entitlement configuration, cache TTL, and version handling after r7 deploy
Inspect authorization decision path for one failing user request to see what entitlements the app evaluated
Confirm directory recorded the 214 role changes correctly and identify any role transition logic that could trigger denials
Establish actual impact scope beyond support proxy counts

next_action.rationale: These three diagnostics directly address the core ambiguity: does the app have stale entitlements, or did the directory sync fail to propagate to the app despite reporting success? Traces show what the app evaluated; IDP claims show what directory sent; service settings show caching/versioning. Together they discriminate between stale_authz_cache vs. role_sync_error vs. idp_claim_error mechanisms.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Traces + IDP claims will reveal whether app is working from old entitlements (supports C03/stale_authz_cache) or received incorrect claims (supports role_sync_error). Service settings will show if a cache or version boundary exists that could explain the 6-hour delay.
